clue.text: Twitch? Preferably keep still and …

definitions.meaning: to twitch is to go birdwatching, chasing rare sightings, so the verb means keeping an eye on the birds
the photographer's old instruction to a sitter, telling them to stay still and look at the lens

explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots run on into 8 across: the photographer's patter continues with 'look happy'. A twitcher is a dedicated British birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitching is the hobby of chasing rare birds, and the photographer's phrase literally tells you to watch a bird.

clue.text: Hi! Whistler granted possibility to lead the Queen's dog

indicators.note: to lead means the rearranged letters come before the royal abbreviation
possibility suggests the letters given could be arranged another way

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Greeting the painter Whistler, who has been allowed to take the monarch's pet out.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler was the American painter; 'possibility' signals the rearrangement and 'to lead' puts it ahead of the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The Westie is a small white Scottish breed of dog.

clue.text: The former Queen leaves 12 — for essayist?

indicators.note: leaves tells us the queen's letters depart from the other word

parts.note: 12 across is the dog, a terrier
the Queen named in the preceding clue, 1 down, is ER

explanation.surface: An old monarch departs from a dog, perhaps in favour of a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: To essay is to attempt, so the question mark says an 'essayist' here is someone who has a go.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so one who essays is one who tries.

clue.text: Scots have parent to master bruise

parts.note: hae is the Scots form of have
ma is mother, a parent
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Scots must make a parent teach the master about an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A haematoma is a swelling of clotted blood under the skin, the medical term for a bad bruise.

clue.text: Gear in which one can work together or die

definitions.meaning: equipment, especially the straps fitted to a draught animal

definitions.text: in which one can work together or die
definitions.meaning: you work in this together with others, and to die in it is to die still working

explanation.walkthrough: Horses work together in harness; 'to die in harness' means to die while still at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness is the set of straps and fittings, tack or gear, for an animal or person.

clue.text: Manner of speaking by heart, maybe

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is an adjective describing such a manner

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A way of talking learnt from memory, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathy voice is a style of speech with audible exhalation.

clue.text: Old poet's first book has page missing

indicators.note: missing tells us the page's letter is dropped from the book

parts.note: a primer is a child's first reading book

explanation.surface: A poet of old had his debut volume with a page torn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' fits because rime is an archaic spelling of rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimer is an archaic spelling of rhymer, a versifier.

clue.text: Spiteful behaviour (as of 12) doesn't start to cause irritation

indicators.note: doesn't start means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: spiteful behaviour is bitchiness, and 12, a terrier, may be a bitch

explanation.surface: Malicious conduct, like a dog's, without a beginning causes annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchiness is a prickly skin sensation, a kind of irritation.

clue.text: … look happy for a second's length

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for a second of time
a mile is a unit of length

explanation.surface: Continuing the photographer's patter: put on a cheerful face for just a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with dots, carrying on from 1 across, the photographer's call to watch the birdie.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin or beam is to look happy, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Cream upset around reverting flower of marsh plant

indicators.note: around tells us the anagrammed letters go round the next piece
upset means the letters of cream are knocked over into a new order
reverting means the river's name is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, crossword shorthand for a river, here the Dee

explanation.surface: Spilt cream around a wilting bloom near some bog plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the cream into RMACE; 'around' wraps it round the river flowing backwards ('reverting'). 'Flower' reads as a bloom but means something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Reed mace is the tall bulrush or cattail of marshes and pond margins.

clue.text: Ecological stimuli are hot stuff

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly, ecological
a pepper is something that peps you up, a stimulus

explanation.surface: Environmental incentives are a fiery business.
explanation.walkthrough: Peppers here are things that pep you up, i.e. stimulants.
explanation.definitionFit: Green peppers are capsicums, and some are hot, a spicy food.

clue.text: Put container in here for fodder

indicators.note: in tells us the container word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bag is a container

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a feed bucket here for the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and green plants used as pasture or animal feed, which is fodder.

clue.text: See 1 down
Wellington's starter, soup

indicators.note: starter means we keep only the beginning of the boot word, cutting off its tail

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot, also called a gumboot

explanation.surface: The Duke of Wellington begins his dinner with a bowl of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' suggests the Duke; it is the rubber boot, a GUMBOOT, and 'starter' drops its final OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is a thick Louisiana stew-like soup thickened with okra.

clue.text: Treatise on gas that turns up in cleaner hydrogen

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed gas goes inside the cleaner

parts.note: a mop is a cleaner

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the gas word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: argon is a noble gas
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A scholarly paper on a gas that shows up in a cleaning product with hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' gives NOGRA (ARGON backwards), placed 'in' MOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A monograph is a detailed scholarly study of one subject, a treatise.

clue.text: Alternative to 8 after 1 across, for example — brie, for example

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, as in 'take, say, Paris'
brie is an example of a cheese

explanation.surface: Another photographer's phrase after the birdie line, illustrated with a soft French cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The photographer says 'watch the birdie', then 'smile', or alternatively the phrase built here.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask sitters to utter this phrase so their mouths form a grin, standing in for asking them to beam.

clue.text: A new Ted in the old Ted? That's how it will all end

definitions.text: That's how it will all end

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters go inside the other

parts.note: Ted Heath, Edward Heath, was a former British prime minister

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A fresh Ted inside the former Ted, and so the universe finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TED into TDE, and with A it goes 'in' the former prime minister's surname; Ted Heath led the UK in 1970-74.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorised end of the universe, when all energy is evenly spread.

clue.text: Assemble and help endlessly and assist

indicators.note: assemble means put together, so the letters that follow are put together in a new order
endlessly means the last letter of help is cut off

explanation.surface: Gather round and pitch in, endlessly helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final letter, and 'Assemble' shuffles the first 'and' with what is left into LENDAH; the second 'and' stays intact at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in and give help is to assist someone, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: I'm after a grandmother as a liar

indicators.note: after tells us the I comes behind the grandmother piece

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
the I of I'm supplies a single letter

explanation.surface: Someone confessing that, like his granny, he tells fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mentions I first, but 'after' says it follows the grandmother piece in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananias is the New Testament figure struck dead for lying, so his name means a fibber.

clue.text: Porter or graduate in academic dress?

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the don

parts.note: a don is a university academic
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Is the college porter really a graduate in a gown?
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' also signals containment, the academic clothing the pieces, so 'in' is doubled up; a college porter guards the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman is a porter stationed at a building's entrance.

clue.text: Put a back on an old storyteller

indicators.note: back tells us the word for put is read in reverse

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it

explanation.surface: Fit a rear piece on an ancient teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the verb round to give ESOP; 'on' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of animal fables, an old teller of stories.

clue.text: Country in exchange with a lot of 23s?

indicators.note: exchange suggests the two letters of in are swapped round
a lot of means we keep most of the word, dropping its end

parts.note: 23 across is my dear fellow's old chap; old chaps are geriatrics

explanation.surface: A nation that trades with many elderly gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' swaps IN to NI; 'a lot of' cuts TRICS from GERIATRICS, the old chaps of 23 across, leaving GERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African nation, so it is a country.

clue.text: Was he leaving the washer-dryer to cook?

indicators.note: leaving tells us those letters depart from the next word

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Was a man leaving the laundry appliance to make dinner?
explanation.walkthrough: Taking W, A, S, H, E away from WASHER leaves R. An oast house is a hop-drying kiln of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in an oven or over a fire.

clue.text: Much cold has its effect, my dear fellow

indicators.note: much hints at a lot of the word, so we lose its opening letter

parts.note: cold weather chaps the skin, so to chap is how cold has its effect

explanation.surface: A heavy chill is taking its toll, old friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much' keeps most of COLD, dropping C to give OLD; cold chaps lips and hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British form of friendly address, used just like 'my good fellow'.

clue.text: Sound of activity to American is good for the soil

definitions.note: the definition describes rather than names the noun, a material that enriches soil

parts.note: a hum is the busy noise of activity

explanation.surface: A busy buzz aimed at an American benefits the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Humus is decomposed organic matter that enriches earth.

clue.text: Anti-Mass disposition?

indicators.note: disposition, read as dis-position, means the letters are placed out of their order

explanation.surface: A temperament opposed to the church's Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: devil-worship is set against the Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil worship is the ultimate opposition to the church service of the Mass.

clue.text: Girl as target, possibly?

definitions.meaning: read as aim plus -ee, like employee or trainee: one who is aimed at

explanation.walkthrough: The suffix -ee marks the person on the receiving end, so an 'aim-ee' would be what is aimed at.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimee is a girl's name, from the French for beloved.

clue.text: Chlorophyll's work in getting people together to 1 across etc?

definitions.meaning: the process by which green pigment lets plants make sugar from light

definitions.text: getting people together to 1 across etc
definitions.meaning: read as photo plus synthesis: assembling a group for a picture

explanation.walkthrough: Synthesis means putting together, so the second reading is assembling people for a photo session.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants use chlorophyll to turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into food, the process the word names.
